newsitem.title: USA: IMF near accord on SDR allocation - Maystadt.
newsitem.headline: IMF near accord on SDR allocation - Maystadt.

text.p: IMF members are near agreement on a new allocation of Special Drawing Rights (SDRs) to provide these to all members, Philippe Maystadt, head of the IMF's policy-making Interim Committee, said on Saturday.

"We are close to an agreement. The range of difference (in opinion on the size of the allocation) is narrow," he told reporters ahead of full ministerial meetings of the International Monetary Fund and World Bank to be held here on Monday.
IMF members have agreed in principle on a one-off allocation of SDRs to bring all members onto an equal footing.
Around 40 countries that joined the Fund recently do not have access to SDRs -- the currency used by the IMF, which its members can draw upon when needed.

IMF managing director Michel Camdessus is seeking an increase that would bring the ratio of SDRs to quotas -- contributions from member states to IMF capital -- to 30 percent. That would be equivalent to an extra 22.4 billion SDRs.
Maystadt, who is also Belgium's finance minister, said, however, that some members believed this was still too high.
The IMF currently has 21 billion SDRs outstanding, so an increase of 22.4 billion would more than double them.
One official said the differences of opinion in the increase in SDRs was narrow, ranging between an increase of 20 billion to an increase of 22.4 billion.
